Build OK; standard test mode PASSES (n1024 test shapes are B=4<fp16_min_batch=16 -> geqrf), but the diff_correctness guard (runs the benchmark shapes) FAILS all 3 n1024 B60 targets (s4/s8/s11): 8/8 inputs wrong. The FP16 two-level path is not numerically correct at OB=128 with the current inner/apply structure -- the wide OB-reflector apply loses the factorization. Need to find why OB=128 breaks (build_Minv/apply width assumptions) before it can be a perf lever.

OB=128 + inner_wmma=0/panel_apply_fused=0 (all applies via cuBLAS bf16). Still FAILS diff_correctness 8/8 on all 3 n1024 B60 targets. So the OB=128 failure is NOT the PAF fusion -- it is the core FP16 two-level apply at width 128: the compact-WY T-inverse (M=L^-1) at OB=128 has much larger off-diagonal entries than at OB=64, and the FP16-W intermediates (W/M/Y stored __half via g_bf16_wf16) overflow/lose precision, corrupting the wide reflector. Need FP32 W/M/Y intermediates (or a hybrid) for the wide OB apply to keep the T-inverse accurate.

Added an FP32-M arm to the bf16 apply driver (set_apply_fp32m_min knob): when w>=cap, W=V^TC computed BF16->FP32, Y=Tp(FP32 T-inverse)@W in FP32, Y->FP16, C-=V@Y BF16; the big GEMMs stay BF16 tensor-core. DIAGNOSTIC config: OB=64 (known-good) + apply_fp32m_min=33 (forces the w=64 outer apply onto FP32-M) + inner_wmma_wmax=16. PASSES diff_correctness CLEAN -> the FP32-M arm is numerically CORRECT. geomean 1666.8us (vs parent 1636; +1.9% from routing inner applies off WMMA via wmax=16, a diagnostic cost). KEY FINDING: the OB=128 diff_correctness failure (residual scaled=533, NOT inf) is NOT the apply precision -- it is a STRUCTURAL bug specific to OB=128 in the two-level loop (build_V/build_Minv/inner-outer interaction at b=128). The FP32-M arm works; OB=128 needs the structural bug found.

Found+fixed a real OB=128 bug: fill_above_panel_R_tiled_kernel's off-diagonal FAST path uses 32 lanes x 2 cols = 64 columns, leaving columns [64,128) UNWRITTEN at OB=128 (garbage R). Gated the fast path on OB<=64 (slow column-strided path handles OB=128). Also set the FP32-M arm's build_Minv to deep nlev (bw<=16). STILL FAILS diff_correctness 8/8; residual WORSENED to scaled=7290 (was 533) -- so there are MULTIPLE latent bugs in the never-before-run OB=128 bf16 two-level path, and the deep-nlev change regressed further. The bf16 path was only ever run at OB=64; OB=128 needs a comprehensive width-assumption audit (PAF kernel OV-fold, apply, build_Minv merge, build_V). FP32-M arm itself is validated correct at w=64 (trial 3).

NEXT: cap PAF fusion at rest<=32 at OB=128 (so only the rest=32 inner panel fuses, rest>=64 -> standalone+cuBLAS), OR fix the PAF smem so rest=64 fits. Built the MULTI-CTA OV panel (panel_factor_ov_multicta_kernel): splits each matrix's standalone OV panel across G CTAs by ROW STRIPE via a COOPERATIVE launch (grid=dim3(G,B)), grid.sync cross-CTA reductions (batched dots over all cols in ONE sync + pivot norm = 2 syncs/col). Cooperative-launch mechanism verified on B200 (296 co-resident CTAs max at this smem; 120 fit). G=1 degenerate (single CTA via the new kernel) PASSES validation and benchmarks 1644 (n1024 ~3308) == parent 1636 -- so the cooperative-launch + grid.sync machinery has NEGLIGIBLE overhead, meaning a correct G=2 should deliver the occupancy win. BUT G=2 currently FAILS correctness (residual 159): a cross-CTA combine bug (the per-CTA dot/norm logic is proven correct by G=1; the bug is in summing gdot/gnrm partials across the 2 CTAs or the gAjc/alpha publish). Committed at G=1 (correct) as a checkpoint. NEXT: instrument + fix the G=2 cross-CTA reduction, then measure grid=120 occupancy vs the 1636 parent.

MULTI-CTA OV panel G=2 now CORRECT (the bug was a missing __syncthreads after the smem panel load -- the load distributes by idx=tid, the col0/dot reads by row, a smem race that G=1 timing masked and G=2 exposed; validates CLEAN). But it BENCHMARKS 1944 (n1024 ~6580us, a 2x REGRESSION vs parent 3300). MEASURED DISPROOF of the multi-CTA-occupancy thesis for this panel: splitting each matrix's panel across 2 CTAs (grid 60->120) HALVES the per-column compute but the panel is BARRIER-LATENCY-bound (sequential column chain), and replacing intra-CTA __syncthreads with cross-CTA cooperative grid.sync barriers (~99 syncs/panel x 15 panels x grid-wide-across-120-CTAs) costs FAR more than the compute saved. G=1 (same kernel, 1 CTA/matrix, grid.sync replacing __syncthreads) was 1644 == parent, confirming grid.sync at 60 CTAs is cheap but the EXTRA barriers + cross-SM coordination at G=2 dominate. So occupancy was NOT the binding constraint; BARRIER LATENCY in the column chain is, and more CTAs make it worse. The cooperative-launch + multi-CTA infra is built+correct+reusable. Open: a multi-CTA split would only pay off if it REDUCED barriers (e.g. column-parallel without per-column grid.sync), not row-split which adds them.

KEY MEASURED FINDING (disproves the occupancy thesis for THIS panel): the n1024 panel is BARRIER-LATENCY-bound on its sequential per-column Householder chain, NOT occupancy-bound. Splitting each matrix across 2 CTAs halves the per-column compute but replaces intra-CTA __syncthreads with cross-CTA cooperative grid.sync barriers (~99 syncs/panel x 15 panels, each grid-wide across 120 CTAs spanning ~60 SMs). The added barrier+cross-SM-coordination cost dominates the compute saved. The idle SMs at grid=60 are NOT the bottleneck; the per-column barrier chain latency is. Combined with the earlier OB-widening result (also regresses), BOTH structural levers the brief named are now measured-disproven for n1024; the parent OB=64 single-CTA config (1636) remains the best.

Built the wide-IB lever: SINGLE-LEVEL OB=IB=64 with the existing FP16-SMEM column-major coop panel (panel_factor_smem_wsp_cm_coop_h_kernel, 129KB at b=64,m=1024 -- fits the 228KB cap; the FP32-smem panel was 266KB). Halves the panel LAUNCH count (16 blocks x1 vs x2). TWO blockers, both measured: (1) PRECISION -- diff_correctness FAILS on s8 (mixed, 5/8 wrong) + s11 (nearrank, 4/8 wrong); the s4 dense passes but THIN (orth scaled 40.1/gate100, factor 11.5/gate20, vs two-level's 0.27/2.7). The 64-wide FP16-smem reflector block accumulates more error than the 32-wide two-level (each column reads FP16-rounded stored values; 64 columns compound it). (2) SPEED -- even s4 (which passes) ran 3528us, SLOWER than parent 3300. Single-level does the whole 64-col within-block trailing serially INSIDE the single-CTA panel (FP16 half8 m-passes), whereas two-level offloads the inner trailing to WMMA TENSOR CORES via PAF. So halving the panel COUNT does NOT reduce total serial-column work (= n columns regardless of IB), and loses the tensor-core inner apply. The wide-IB lever REGRESSES on both axes. Reverting to the parent config.
